OCCUPATIONAL NOISE EXPOSURE AND HEARING CONSERVATION — INFORMATION SHEET
Prepared for Jordan Lee · Acme Innovations LLC

ABOUT THIS OCCUPATIONAL NOISE EXPOSURE INFORMATION SHEET
This Occupational Noise Exposure and Hearing Conservation Information Sheet describes California's Cal/OSHA regulation controlling workplace noise exposure, Article 105 of the General Industry Safety Orders (8 Cal. Code Regs. §§ 5095–5100), as those requirements relate to the working relationship between Jordan Lee and Acme Innovations LLC.

It summarizes selected requirements of that regulation: which workplaces and industries are covered and which are exempt from specific provisions, the action level and permissible exposure limits that trigger the regulation's duties, the hearing conservation program and noise monitoring requirements, the audiometric testing program, the response required when an employee experiences a standard threshold shift in hearing, the duty to provide hearing protectors, employee training and information-access requirements, and recordkeeping and records-access requirements.

Acme Innovations LLC has identified Pat Morgan as the person responsible for Acme Innovations LLC's hearing conservation program, where one is required.

This information sheet is not itself Acme Innovations LLC's hearing conservation program, does not itself satisfy any written-program or recordkeeping requirement of Article 105, and does not determine whether any particular job, work area, or noise level at Acme Innovations LLC triggers the regulation's requirements.

WHICH WORKPLACES ARTICLE 105 COVERS, AND THE LIMITS OF ITS INDUSTRY EXEMPTION
Article 105 establishes requirements for controlling occupational exposures to noise. Agriculture, construction, and oil and gas well drilling and servicing operations are exempt from the provisions of Sections 5097 through 5100 — that is, from the hearing conservation program, audiometric testing, hearing protector, and recordkeeping requirements. The regulation's text does not list Section 5096, which sets the permissible noise exposure limits, among the sections from which those industries are exempted.

[Verified — checked 2026-09-06]
  "(a) Scope and Application. Article 105 establishes requirements for controlling occupational exposures to noise. Agriculture, construction, and oil and gas well drilling and servicing operations are exempt from the provisions of Sections 5097 through 5100."
  — 8 Cal. Code Regs. § 5095(a) (Occupational Noise — General), 8 CCR § 5095(a), scope and application; industry exemption (https://www.dir.ca.gov/title8/5095.html)
  Known gap: This clause states 8 Cal. Code Regs. § 5095(a)'s own scope and exemption language; because that subsection exempts agriculture, construction, and oil and gas well drilling and servicing operations only from "the provisions of Sections 5097 through 5100," and does not name Section 5096, this document does not conclude that those industries are exempt from Section 5096's exposure-limit and control-measure duties, and it does not resolve how the exemption interacts with any industry-specific safety order that may separately govern noise in those sectors. It also does not determine whether any particular employer or work area falls within an exempt classification.

THE ACTION LEVEL AND CRITERION SOUND LEVEL THAT TRIGGER THE REGULATION'S DUTIES
Article 105 defines the "action level" as an 8-hour time-weighted average of 85 decibels measured on the A-scale, slow response, or equivalently, a dose of fifty percent. It defines the "criterion sound level" — the reference level used in calculating an employee's noise dose — as a sound level of 90 decibels. The action level of 85 dBA (TWA) is the threshold at which Article 105's hearing conservation program, monitoring, audiometric testing, and training duties are triggered for a given employee.

[Verified — checked 2026-09-06]
  "Action Level. An 8-hour time-weighted average of 85 decibels measured on the A-scale, slow response, or equivalently, a dose of fifty percent."
  — 8 Cal. Code Regs. § 5095(b) (Occupational Noise — Definitions), 8 CCR § 5095(b), definition of "Action Level" (https://www.dir.ca.gov/title8/5095.html)
  "Criterion Sound Level. A sound level of 90 decibels."
  — 8 Cal. Code Regs. § 5095(b) (Occupational Noise — Definitions), 8 CCR § 5095(b), definition of "Criterion Sound Level" (https://www.dir.ca.gov/title8/5095.html)
  Known gap: This clause reproduces only the two defined terms most directly tied to when the regulation's duties apply. Section 5095(b) defines additional terms used elsewhere in Article 105 (including "audiogram," "audiologist," "baseline audiogram," "representative exposure," and "sound level meter") that this clause does not restate, and it does not describe the technical dose-calculation methodology in Appendix A referenced elsewhere in the regulation.

PERMISSIBLE NOISE EXPOSURE LIMITS AND THE REQUIRED ORDER OF CONTROLS
Section 5096 requires protection against the effects of noise exposure whenever sound levels exceed those set out in the regulation's Table N-1, measured on the A-scale of a standard sound level meter at slow response. Table N-1 permits a sound level of 90 dBA for a full 8-hour workday, with the permitted exposure duration shortening as the sound level rises (for example, 95 dBA is permitted for 4 hours, and 100 dBA for 2 hours). Where sound levels exceed the table, feasible administrative or engineering controls must be used first; personal protective equipment is required only if those controls fail to bring sound levels within the table's limits. Noise with maxima recurring at intervals of one second or less is treated as continuous, and exposure to impulsive or impact noise may not exceed 140 dB peak sound pressure level.

[Verified — checked 2026-09-06]
  "(a) Protection against the effects of noise exposure shall be provided when the sound levels exceed those shown in Table N-1 of this section when measured on the A-scale of a standard sound level meter at slow response."
  — 8 Cal. Code Regs. § 5096(a) (Exposure Limits for Noise), 8 CCR § 5096(a), general exposure-limit trigger (https://www.dir.ca.gov/title8/5096.html)
  "(b) When employees are subjected to sound levels exceeding those listed in Table N-1 of this section, feasible administrative or engineering controls shall be utilized. If such controls fail to reduce sound levels within the levels of the table, personal protective equipment shall be provided and used to reduce sound levels within the levels of the table."
  — 8 Cal. Code Regs. § 5096(b) (Exposure Limits for Noise), 8 CCR § 5096(b), hierarchy of controls: engineering/administrative controls before PPE (https://www.dir.ca.gov/title8/5096.html)
  "90........... 8-0...... 8.00"
  — 8 Cal. Code Regs. § 5096, Table N-1 (Exposure Limits for Noise), 8 CCR § 5096, Table N-1 — permitted duration at 90 dBA (quoted exactly as the source's own dot-leader table formatting renders it: sound level 90 dBA, permitted duration 8 hours 0 minutes, i.e. 8.00 hours) (https://www.dir.ca.gov/title8/5096.html)
  "(c) If the variations in noise level involve maxima at intervals of 1 second or less, the noise is to be considered continuous."
  — 8 Cal. Code Regs. § 5096(c) (Exposure Limits for Noise), 8 CCR § 5096(c), continuous-noise treatment (https://www.dir.ca.gov/title8/5096.html)
  "(d) Exposure to impulsive or impact noise should not exceed 140 dB peak sound pressure level."
  — 8 Cal. Code Regs. § 5096(d) (Exposure Limits for Noise), 8 CCR § 5096(d), impulsive/impact noise peak limit (https://www.dir.ca.gov/title8/5096.html)
  Known gap: This clause quotes Table N-1's anchor value (90 dBA for 8 hours) rather than reproducing the full table, which sets a permitted duration for every integer sound level from 90 through 115 dBA; it does not reproduce the table's footnoted formula for combining two or more periods of exposure at different sound levels (the sum of each period's exposure-to-permitted-duration ratio), which the regulation directs be used when noise levels vary during a shift. The quoted Table N-1 row preserves the source's own dot-leader table formatting exactly as published: "90........... 8-0...... 8.00" states that a sound level of 90 dBA is permitted for a duration of 8 hours 0 minutes (8.00 hours) -- the dots are typographic table-column leaders in the source, not part of the substantive text.

THE HEARING CONSERVATION PROGRAM REQUIREMENT AND NOISE MONITORING
An employer must administer a continuing, effective hearing conservation program whenever employee noise exposures equal or exceed an 8-hour time-weighted average of 85 decibels (the action level), or equivalently a dose of fifty percent. When information indicates that an employee's exposure may equal or exceed that level, the employer must obtain noise measurements for the employees who may be exposed at or above it, using area or personal sampling. Affected employees or their representatives must be given an opportunity to observe any noise measurements taken under this requirement, and each employee exposed at or above the action level must be notified of the monitoring results.

[Verified — checked 2026-09-06]
  "(a) General. The employer shall administer a continuing, effective hearing conservation program, as described in this section, whenever employee noise exposures equal or exceed an 8-hour time-weighted average sound level (TWA) of 85 decibels measured on the A-scale (slow response) or, equivalently, a dose of fifty percent."
  — 8 Cal. Code Regs. § 5097(a) (Hearing Conservation Program — General), 8 CCR § 5097(a), duty to administer a hearing conservation program (https://www.dir.ca.gov/title8/5097.html)
  "(1) When information indicates that any employee's exposure may equal or exceed an 8-hour time-weighted average of 85 decibels, the employer shall obtain measurements for employees who may be exposed at or above that level."
  — 8 Cal. Code Regs. § 5097(b)(1) (Hearing Conservation Program — Monitoring), 8 CCR § 5097(b)(1), duty to obtain exposure measurements (https://www.dir.ca.gov/title8/5097.html)
  "The employer shall provide affected employees or their representatives with an opportunity to observe any measurements of employee noise exposure which are conducted pursuant to this section."
  — 8 Cal. Code Regs. § 5097(b)(4) (Hearing Conservation Program — Monitoring), 8 CCR § 5097(b)(4), employee opportunity to observe monitoring (https://www.dir.ca.gov/title8/5097.html)
  "The employer shall notify each employee exposed at or above the action level of the results of the monitoring."
  — 8 Cal. Code Regs. § 5097(b)(5) (Hearing Conservation Program — Monitoring), 8 CCR § 5097(b)(5), duty to notify employees of monitoring results (https://www.dir.ca.gov/title8/5097.html)
  Known gap: This clause states the program's overall trigger and the core monitoring, observation, and notification duties in Section 5097(a) and (b)(1), (b)(4), and (b)(5). It does not reproduce the more technical monitoring-method requirements in (b)(2) (when area sampling versus personal sampling must be used, the 80–130 dB integration range, and instrument calibration) or the circumstances requiring re-monitoring under (b)(3).

THE AUDIOMETRIC TESTING PROGRAM: BASELINE AUDIOGRAMS AND ANNUAL TESTING
An employer must establish and maintain an audiometric testing program, at no cost to employees, making audiometric testing available to every employee whose noise exposure equals or exceeds the action level. For each such employee, the employer must establish a valid baseline audiogram against which later audiograms are compared; testing for that baseline must be preceded by at least 14 hours without exposure to workplace noise (a requirement that may instead be met by wearing hearing protectors that reduce the employee's exposure to 80 dBA or below during that period). Baseline testing must generally be made available within 6 months of an employee's first exposure at or above the action level (within 1 year if a mobile test van is used), and, after the baseline, the employer must obtain a new audiogram for each covered employee at least annually.

[Verified — checked 2026-09-06]
  "(1) The employer shall establish and maintain an audiometric testing program as provided in this section by making audiometric testing available to all employees whose exposures equal or exceed the action level."
  — 8 Cal. Code Regs. § 5097(c)(1) (Hearing Conservation Program — Audiometric Testing), 8 CCR § 5097(c)(1), duty to make audiometric testing available (https://www.dir.ca.gov/title8/5097.html)
  "(2) The program shall be provided at no cost to employees."
  — 8 Cal. Code Regs. § 5097(c)(2) (Hearing Conservation Program — Audiometric Testing), 8 CCR § 5097(c)(2), testing provided at no cost (https://www.dir.ca.gov/title8/5097.html)
  "The employer shall establish for each employee exposed at or above the action level a valid baseline audiogram against which subsequent audiograms can be compared."
  — 8 Cal. Code Regs. § 5097(c)(5) (Hearing Conservation Program — Audiometric Testing), 8 CCR § 5097(c)(5), baseline audiogram requirement (https://www.dir.ca.gov/title8/5097.html)
  "Testing to establish a baseline audiogram shall be preceded by at least 14 hours without exposure to workplace noise. This requirement may be met by wearing hearing protectors which will reduce the employee's exposure to a sound level of 80 dBA or below."
  — 8 Cal. Code Regs. § 5097(c)(6) (Hearing Conservation Program — Audiometric Testing), 8 CCR § 5097(c)(6), 14-hour quiet period before baseline testing (https://www.dir.ca.gov/title8/5097.html)
  "Audiometric tests shall be made available to employees by June 1, 1983 or within 6 months of an employee's first exposure at or above the action level, except that where a mobile test van is used to conduct the audiometric test, the test shall be made available within one year of an employee's first exposure at or above the action level provided that all such employees are given an opportunity for testing."
  — 8 Cal. Code Regs. § 5097(c)(8) (Hearing Conservation Program — Audiometric Testing), 8 CCR § 5097(c)(8), timing for baseline testing availability (https://www.dir.ca.gov/title8/5097.html)
  "At least annually after obtaining the baseline audiogram, the employer shall obtain a new audiogram for each employee exposed at or above the action level."
  — 8 Cal. Code Regs. § 5097(c)(10) (Hearing Conservation Program — Audiometric Testing), 8 CCR § 5097(c)(10), annual audiogram requirement (https://www.dir.ca.gov/title8/5097.html)
  Known gap: This clause covers the core testing-program obligations in Section 5097(c)(1), (2), (5), (6), (8), and (10); it does not restate the technician-qualification requirements in (c)(3), the audiogram technical standards in (c)(4) (Appendix B), the historical June 1, 1983 compliance date noted in (c)(8), or the mobile-test-van interim hearing-protector proviso in (c)(9).

STANDARD THRESHOLD SHIFT: DEFINITION, NOTICE, AND REQUIRED FOLLOW-UP
A "standard threshold shift" is defined as a change in hearing threshold, relative to an employee's baseline audiogram, averaging 10 dB or more at 2000, 3000, and 4000 Hz in either ear. If a comparison of an employee's annual audiogram to the baseline audiogram shows a standard threshold shift, the employee must be informed of that fact in writing within 21 days of the determination. Unless a physician determines the shift is not work-related or aggravated by occupational noise exposure, the employer must ensure follow-up steps are taken: an employee not already using hearing protectors must be fitted with them, trained in their use and care, and required to use them, and an employee already using hearing protectors must be refitted and retrained and, if necessary, provided with protectors offering greater attenuation.

[Verified — checked 2026-09-06]
  "As used in this section, a standard threshold shift is a change in hearing threshold relative to the baseline audiogram of an average of 10 dB or more at 2000, 3000 and 4000 Hz in either ear."
  — 8 Cal. Code Regs. § 5097(d)(8) (Hearing Conservation Program — Evaluation of Audiogram), 8 CCR § 5097(d)(8), definition of "standard threshold shift" (https://www.dir.ca.gov/title8/5097.html)
  "If a comparison of the annual audiogram to the baseline audiogram indicates a standard threshold shift as defined by Section 5097(d)(8), the employee shall be informed of this fact, in writing, within 21 days of the determination."
  — 8 Cal. Code Regs. § 5097(d)(4) (Hearing Conservation Program — Evaluation of Audiogram), 8 CCR § 5097(d)(4), 21-day written notice of a standard threshold shift (https://www.dir.ca.gov/title8/5097.html)
  "Unless a physician determines that the standard threshold shift is not work related or aggravated by occupational noise exposure, the employer shall ensure that the following steps are taken when a standard threshold shift occurs:"
  — 8 Cal. Code Regs. § 5097(d)(5) (Hearing Conservation Program — Evaluation of Audiogram), 8 CCR § 5097(d)(5), follow-up steps required after a standard threshold shift (https://www.dir.ca.gov/title8/5097.html)
  "An employee not using hearing protectors shall be fitted with hearing protectors, trained in their use and care, and required to use them; and"
  — 8 Cal. Code Regs. § 5097(d)(5)(A) (Hearing Conservation Program — Evaluation of Audiogram), 8 CCR § 5097(d)(5)(A), fitting and training an employee not yet using protectors (https://www.dir.ca.gov/title8/5097.html)
  Known gap: This clause states the standard-threshold-shift definition in Section 5097(d)(8), the 21-day written-notice duty in (d)(4), and the general follow-up obligation in (d)(5) and (d)(5)(A). It does not reproduce every follow-up sub-step in (d)(5)(B) through (D) (referral for clinical evaluation and notice of a suspected unrelated ear pathology) in full, the audiogram re-evaluation and substitution rules in (d)(2), (d)(6), and (d)(7), or the age-correction (presbycusis) procedure in (d)(9) and Appendix F, which may affect whether a given audiogram change is treated as a standard threshold shift.

HEARING PROTECTORS: AVAILABILITY, COST, SELECTION, AND REQUIRED ATTENUATION
An employer must make hearing protectors available, at no cost, to every employee exposed to an 8-hour time-weighted average of 85 decibels or greater, and must replace them as necessary. Employees who are given a choice must be allowed to select their hearing protectors from a variety of suitable types the employer provides. Hearing protectors must attenuate an employee's exposure to at least an 8-hour time-weighted average of 90 decibels, as required for the exposure-limit control hierarchy under Section 5096(b); for an employee who has experienced a standard threshold shift, hearing protectors must instead attenuate exposure to 85 decibels or below.

[Verified — checked 2026-09-06]
  "(1) Employers shall make hearing protectors available to all employees exposed to an 8-hour time-weighted average of 85 decibels or greater at no cost to the employees. Hearing protectors shall be replaced as necessary."
  — 8 Cal. Code Regs. § 5098(a)(1) (Hearing Protectors — General), 8 CCR § 5098(a)(1), duty to provide hearing protectors at no cost (https://www.dir.ca.gov/title8/5098.html)
  "(3) Employees shall be given the opportunity to select their hearing protectors from a variety of suitable hearing protectors provided by the employer."
  — 8 Cal. Code Regs. § 5098(a)(3) (Hearing Protectors — General), 8 CCR § 5098(a)(3), employee's opportunity to select from a variety of protectors (https://www.dir.ca.gov/title8/5098.html)
  "(2) Hearing protectors must attenuate employee exposure at least to an 8-hour time-weighted average of 90 decibels as required by Section 5096(b)."
  — 8 Cal. Code Regs. § 5098(b)(2) (Hearing Protectors — Attenuation), 8 CCR § 5098(b)(2), 90 dBA required attenuation level (https://www.dir.ca.gov/title8/5098.html)
  "(3) For employees who have experienced a standard threshold shift, hearing protectors must attenuate employee exposures to an 8-hour time-weighted average of 85 decibels or below."
  — 8 Cal. Code Regs. § 5098(b)(3) (Hearing Protectors — Attenuation), 8 CCR § 5098(b)(3), 85 dBA attenuation level after a standard threshold shift (https://www.dir.ca.gov/title8/5098.html)
  Known gap: This clause states the core availability, cost, selection, and attenuation-level duties in Section 5098(a)(1), (a)(3), and (b)(2)-(3). It does not restate the specific circumstances under which hearing protector use becomes mandatory rather than merely available under (a)(2)(A)-(B), the employer's training and proper-fitting duties in (a)(4)-(5), or the attenuation-evaluation methodology in (b)(1) and Appendix E that this document does not reproduce.

EMPLOYEE TRAINING AND ACCESS TO THE REGULATION'S TEXT
An employer must institute a training program for every employee exposed to noise at or above an 8-hour time-weighted average of 85 dBA and must ensure employee participation in it. The training must be repeated annually for each employee included in the hearing conservation program. Separately, the employer must make available to affected employees or their representatives copies of Article 105 itself, and must post a copy of it in the workplace.

[Verified — checked 2026-09-06]
  "(1) The employer shall institute a training program for all employees who are exposed to noise at or above an 8-hour time-weighted average of 85 dBA, and shall ensure employee participation in such program."
  — 8 Cal. Code Regs. § 5099(a)(1) (Training Program — General), 8 CCR § 5099(a)(1), duty to institute and ensure participation in training (https://www.dir.ca.gov/title8/5099.html)
  "(2) The training program shall be repeated annually for each employee included in the hearing conservation program."
  — 8 Cal. Code Regs. § 5099(a)(2) (Training Program — General), 8 CCR § 5099(a)(2), annual repetition of training (https://www.dir.ca.gov/title8/5099.html)
  "(1) The employer shall make available to affected employees or their representatives copies of Article 105 and shall also post a copy in the workplace."
  — 8 Cal. Code Regs. § 5099(b)(1) (Training Program — Access to Information), 8 CCR § 5099(b)(1), duty to provide and post the regulation's text (https://www.dir.ca.gov/title8/5099.html)
  Known gap: This clause states the training-program trigger and annual-repetition duty in Section 5099(a)(1)-(2), and the duty to make Article 105's text available and post it in (b)(1). It does not restate the specific training-content topics listed in (a)(3)(A)-(C) (the effects of noise on hearing; the purpose, types, and use of hearing protectors; and the purpose of audiometric testing), and it does not address the employer's separate duties in (b)(2)-(3) to pass along federal OSHA informational materials and to make training materials available to specified government representatives upon request.

RECORDKEEPING: RETENTION PERIODS, ACCESS, AND TRANSFER ON CHANGE OF EMPLOYER
An employer must keep an accurate record of every employee exposure measurement required under the monitoring provisions. Noise exposure measurement records must be retained for 2 years, while audiometric test records must be retained for the duration of the affected employee's employment. All records required under this recordkeeping section must be made available on request to employees, former employees, an individual employee's designated representative, and any authorized representative of the Chief of the Division. If the employer ceases doing business, it must transfer these records to the successor employer, who must then retain them for whatever portion of the applicable retention period remains.

[Verified — checked 2026-09-06]
  "The employer shall maintain an accurate record of all employee exposure measurements required by Section 5097(b)."
  — 8 Cal. Code Regs. § 5100(a) (Recordkeeping — Exposure Measurements), 8 CCR § 5100(a), duty to record exposure measurements (https://www.dir.ca.gov/title8/5100.html)
  "(1) Noise exposure measurement records shall be retained for 2 years."
  — 8 Cal. Code Regs. § 5100(d)(1)-(2) (Recordkeeping — Record Retention), 8 CCR § 5100(d)(1)-(2), retention periods for exposure and audiometric records (https://www.dir.ca.gov/title8/5100.html)
  "(2) Audiometric test records shall be retained for the duration of the affected employee's employment."
  — 8 Cal. Code Regs. § 5100(d)(2) (Recordkeeping — Record Retention), 8 CCR § 5100(d)(2), audiometric record retention for duration of employment (https://www.dir.ca.gov/title8/5100.html)
  "All records required by this section shall be provided upon request to employees, former employees, representatives designated by the individual employee and any authorized representative of the Chief of the Division."
  — 8 Cal. Code Regs. § 5100(e) (Recordkeeping — Access to Records), 8 CCR § 5100(e), employee and former-employee access to records (https://www.dir.ca.gov/title8/5100.html)
  "If the employer ceases to do business, the employer shall transfer to the successor employer all records required to be maintained by this section, and the successor employer shall retain them for the remainder of the period prescribed in Section 5100(d)."
  — 8 Cal. Code Regs. § 5100(f) (Recordkeeping — Transfer of Records), 8 CCR § 5100(f), duty to transfer records to a successor employer (https://www.dir.ca.gov/title8/5100.html)
  Known gap: This clause states the general exposure-measurement recordkeeping duty in Section 5100(a), the two differing retention periods in (d)(1)-(2), the access right in (e), and the business-transfer duty in (f). It does not restate the specific audiogram record-content requirements in (b)(2)(A)-(E) (employee name and job classification, audiogram date, examiner's name, calibration date, and most recent exposure assessment), the audiometric-test-room measurement recordkeeping duty in (c), or the substance of the cross-referenced access procedures in 8 Cal. Code Regs. §§ 3204(a)-(h), which this document does not independently verify or reproduce.

expectedJSON.body: An employer must administer a continuing, effective hearing conservation program whenever employee noise exposures equal or exceed an 8-hour time-weighted average of 85 decibels (the action level), or equivalently a dose of fifty percent. When information indicates that an employee's exposure may equal or exceed that level, the employer must obtain noise measurements for the employees who may be exposed at or above it, using area or personal sampling. Affected employees or their representatives must be given an opportunity to observe any noise measurements taken under this requirement, and each employee exposed at or above the action level must be notified of the monitoring results.

expectedJSON.body: An employer must establish and maintain an audiometric testing program, at no cost to employees, making audiometric testing available to every employee whose noise exposure equals or exceeds the action level. For each such employee, the employer must establish a valid baseline audiogram against which later audiograms are compared; testing for that baseline must be preceded by at least 14 hours without exposure to workplace noise (a requirement that may instead be met by wearing hearing protectors that reduce the employee's exposure to 80 dBA or below during that period). Baseline testing must generally be made available within 6 months of an employee's first exposure at or above the action level (within 1 year if a mobile test van is used), and, after the baseline, the employer must obtain a new audiogram for each covered employee at least annually.

expectedJSON.body: A "standard threshold shift" is defined as a change in hearing threshold, relative to an employee's baseline audiogram, averaging 10 dB or more at 2000, 3000, and 4000 Hz in either ear. If a comparison of an employee's annual audiogram to the baseline audiogram shows a standard threshold shift, the employee must be informed of that fact in writing within 21 days of the determination. Unless a physician determines the shift is not work-related or aggravated by occupational noise exposure, the employer must ensure follow-up steps are taken: an employee not already using hearing protectors must be fitted with them, trained in their use and care, and required to use them, and an employee already using hearing protectors must be refitted and retrained and, if necessary, provided with protectors offering greater attenuation.

Employees who are given a choice must be allowed to select their hearing protectors from a variety of suitable types the employer provides. Hearing protectors must attenuate an employee's exposure to at least an 8-hour time-weighted average of 90 decibels, as required for the exposure-limit control hierarchy under Section 5096(b); for an employee who has experienced a standard threshold shift, hearing protectors must instead attenuate exposure to 85 decibels or below.

expectedJSON.body: An employer must keep an accurate record of every employee exposure measurement required under the monitoring provisions. If the employer ceases doing business, it must transfer these records to the successor employer, who must then retain them for whatever portion of the applicable retention period remains.
